title: AAV9-hSynI-WWOX: no independent-laboratory measurement of the endpoint exists and none is likely to be found; what is open is whether the untested post-onset exterior is a boundary or an artefact of the null model, and a hypomorph design with a neonatal positive-control arm settles it
source: scientist-c, task MODULE-C8-20261024; handoff row Q-R-01 (disease-models/wwox/analysis/mechanism_intervention_map.md:403); the bound PMID 42128308 is a Review by PubMed article type and measures nothing, so an independent measurement of it is ill-posed; the measurements are PMID 34747138 and PMID 42422765, manifests present, one laboratory; established 2026-10-23 in disease-models/wwox/research/module_batch_selection_scientist-c_20261023.md, PubMed title/abstract screen that day returned no second-laboratory study
causal_statement: IPOTESI: the endpoint the row rests on is survival to a fixed census age, and spike-wave discharge rate on continuous ECoG, after vector delivery in a Wwox-deficient mouse; the published interval of delivery is the interval that was tested and not a demonstrated boundary, and the source's own authors attribute the untested exterior to model-specific constraints. The discriminating design therefore runs delayed, post-onset delivery in a long-surviving hypomorphic allele rather than the null, and carries a within-study neonatal arm as a positive control, so that a null result in the new model can be told apart from a model that does not respond at all.
falsifier: delayed, post-onset delivery in the hypomorph matching the within-study neonatal arm on survival and spike-wave discharge rate refutes the window as the row's limiting risk; benefit confined to the neonatal arm while the hypomorph itself responds neonatally establishes the window as a real boundary; absence of benefit in both arms of the hypomorph, with the published effect reproduced in the null, refutes the hypomorph as a competent test system rather than the window; a second-laboratory vector study of the same endpoints, in either direction, refutes the single-laboratory dependence
transfer_limit: every endpoint transfers only as the mouse measurement it is, for the allele and the census age measured; nothing here transfers to human efficacy, to the developmental trajectory or to the prenatal progenitor limb, which the neuronal route does not reach; the published safety statement about ganglion toxicity is a class-level statement from a review and is NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; no dose, administration or suitability statement is made, and any dose arm is specified only as a fraction of the source's own high arm, never in absolute units. Not medical advice.
